yes: The sentence mentions or comments on the named aspect category of the restaurant, even briefly or with neutral sentiment.
no: Nothing in the sentence concerns the named aspect category; it is only about other aspects of the restaurant or the visit.
food: What was eaten or drunk: dishes, ingredients, desserts and drinks (wine, beer, coffee, cocktails), their taste, quality, freshness, temperature or preparation, and the meal itself (breakfast, lunch, dinner). Portion size counts as miscellaneous, not food.
menu: What the restaurant offers rather than how it tasted: the menu or wine list, the range, selection or variety of dishes and drinks, specials, prix-fixe or tasting options, and whether items are available.
staff: The people who work there, such as waiters, waitresses, servers, hosts, bartenders, managers, chefs, owners or a DJ, and anything a staff member does: how they behave (friendly, rude, knowledgeable, helpful) and how they serve you (attentive, checking on the table, forgetting an order, being slow). When a person who works there is the one acting, choose staff rather than service.
service: The service in general, not tied to a particular person: the word service itself, how fast or slowly food, drinks or the check arrived, waits for food, dishes coming out in the wrong order, and delivery or takeout. If a waiter, server or other staff member is the one being described, that is staff, not service. Reservations and waiting for a table usually count as miscellaneous.
ambience: The atmosphere and feel of the room: decor, art, lighting, music, live entertainment, noise, mood, vibe, and how romantic, cozy, trendy or comfortable it feels.
place: The restaurant as a physical venue: the place or restaurant as such, its location, neighbourhood or view, and its spaces (dining rooms, the bar, the counter, the kitchen, tables and seating, the terrace, bathrooms), including their size and how crowded or packed they are.
price: Money: prices, the cost of dishes or the meal, the bill or check, the tip, dollar amounts, and whether it was cheap, expensive, overpriced or worth the money.
miscellaneous: Any other aspect not covered by the concrete categories: portion sizes, reservations and getting a table, the time or occasion of the visit, lines, who the other diners are, restaurant policies, general value or deals, and the overall experience.
